title: Ex Vivo Mouse Paired Single-Gonad Screening for Phenotypical Characterization
author: Estermann, Rodriguez, et al.

steps.title: Prepare agar slabs in resin molds
steps.instruction: Generate agar slabs using the 3D‑printed resin molds for single‑gonad culture.

substeps.instruction: Measure 1.5 mg bactoagar into a 20 mL Pyrex Erlenmeyer flask and add 10 mL complete media; cover with film.
Heat 40 mL deionized, filtered water in a 100 mL beaker in a microwave for 1 min until boiling; set aside (handle with care).

Microwave‑heat the agar‑media mixture in the Erlenmeyer in short intervals; stop when bubbles appear, swirl to remove bubbles, and continue heating until the agar is completely dissolved (watch bubble size; small white particles may remain).
Place the hot Erlenmeyer flask into the beaker of hot water (water bath).
Spray the flask with ethanol and place it in the hood.
Pipette 90 µL of the hot agar solution into each resin mold, forming a dome; avoid bubbles (10 mL agar solution yields ~36 wells; use at least 12 molds to make several slabs).
Allow the agar to solidify, then remove each slab with a mini spatula and place it in a 48‑well plate with the dome side down and the groove side up.
If the agar solidifies completely in the Erlenmeyer, re‑heat in the microwave in short intervals until liquid again.

Repeat the dispensing and placement until all inner wells are filled (1 gonad per well, 2 wells per fetal gonadal pair). Use inner wells to minimize evaporation; a 48‑well plate can hold 12 gonadal pairs per plate.

steps.title: Fix and sucrose infiltrate gonads
steps.instruction: Remove culture media and fix the cultured gonads, then infiltrate with sucrose before freezing.

substeps.instruction: Remove the culture media from each well and add 500 µL freshly prepared 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1X PBS.
Fix overnight (16–18 h) at 4 °C or for 1 h at room temperature.
Discard fixative and wash three times with 1X PBS, 10 min each at room temperature.
Replace PBS with 30 % sucrose in 1X PBS and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Embed gonads in OCT and freeze
steps.instruction: Transfer sucrose‑treated gonads into OCT blocks and store at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Place each gonad into a cryo‑mold (10 mm × 10 mm × 5 mm) filled with OCT compound; use a needle to push the tissue to the bottom and orient it as desired.
Mark the right‑top corner of the cryo‑mold with a permanent marker (this mark transfers to the OCT block for orientation).
Transfer the OCT‑filled cryo‑molds to a –80 °C freezer for at least several hours (or until solid).

steps.title: Cryosection gonads onto slides
steps.instruction: Section frozen OCT blocks and collect sections on positively‑charged slides.

substeps.instruction: Remove OCT blocks from –80 °C, place them in the cryostat and let equilibrate.
Section at –20 °C to obtain 10 µm thick sections.
Collect consecutive sections on 4–5 positively‑charged glass slides, alternating slides; annotate the blue‑corner orientation on each slide for later identification.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval (optional)
steps.instruction: Perform citrate‑based antigen retrieval on sections if required by the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Prepare pre‑warmed citrate‑based antigen retrieval solution (Vector Laboratories).
Microwave slides in the solution at 10 % power for 20 min, then let cool at room temperature for 30 min.
If not needed, skip this step.

steps.title: Block and primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Block, permeabilize, and incubate sections with primary antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Remove retrieval solution (if used) and rinse with 1X PBS at room temperature.
Transfer slides to the Sequenza manual immunohistochemistry system (or staining tray) with 500 µL PBS.
Block and permeabilize in 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in 1X PBS containing 5 % normal donkey serum for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate with primary antibodies diluted in the same blocking buffer overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation and washes
steps.instruction: Wash and apply secondary antibodies, then perform final washes.

substeps.instruction: Wash slides three times with 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in 1X PBS.
Incubate with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash once with 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in 1X PBS and twice with 1X PBS.
If autofluorescence is problematic (e.g., Leydig cells), treat with TrueView Autofluorescence Quenching Kit for 3 min, then wash 10 min with 500 µL 1X PBS.

steps.title: Counterstain, mount, and image
steps.instruction: Apply DAPI, mount coverslips, and acquire images.

substeps.instruction: Counterstain sections with DAPI.
Mount using ProLong™ Diamond Antifade Mountant and let harden for at least overnight.
Image the stained sections on a confocal microscope (e.g., Ki‑67 proliferation and cleaved caspase‑3 apoptosis markers).

description: In mice, gonadal sex differentiation occurs during a narrow developmental window between embryonic day E11.5 and E13.5. During this period, the bipotential gonad undergoes rapid cellular and molecular changes that lead to the establishment of either testis or ovary fate. Because these events occur in utero, direct experimental manipulation and screening during this stage can be technically challenging. To address these limitations, several ex vivo culture systems have been developed to maintain embryonic gonads outside the embryo while preserving their structure and differentiation capacity.2,3,4,5 The current gold-standard methodology for mouse fetal gonadal culture, developed by Capel and Batchvarov,2 while widely adopted, this approach cultures multiple gonads within a single agar slab in 10 mm Petri dishes, compromising the individuality of each sample, and requiring substantial amounts of media and reagents. In addition, the original metal molds are difficult to fabricate and typically must be obtained from the originating laboratory, limiting accessibility and reproducibility. In this protocol, we provide 3D-printable molds optimized for single-gonad culture in standard 48-well plates, along with detailed guidance on resin mold printing, gonad dissection, agar slab preparation, paired culture setup, and treatment application. We also describe downstream phenotypic assessments, including immunostaining, transcriptomic analysis, and metabolic measurements in both tissue and culture media. This protocol is used to investigate the effects of different treatments on fetal gonadal cell differentiation ex vivo. The outlined protocol utilizes E11.5 or E12.5 fetal gonads from wild type C57BL/6 mice (Jackson Laboratory #000664), but the protocol can also be applied to fetal gonads from transgenic mice. This protocol is a modified version of the agar slab gonad culture method by Capel and Batchvarov.2
